key_insight: DrugCon detects contradictory trial conclusions about the same drug–disease association and identifies study-level differences that may explain the disagreement.
clinical_relevance: The framework could support evidence review by highlighting conflicting efficacy claims and differences in trial populations, outcomes, or treatment exposure.
method: Uses an LLM to extract conclusions from randomized controlled trial abstracts and link claims about the same drug–disease association.
Applies counterfactual reasoning to detect contradictions.
Explains disagreements using a taxonomy of 10 study-level factors.
evidence_signal: From 224,756 RCT abstracts, researchers built an annotated benchmark of 542 contradictory claim pairs from 819 abstracts; DrugCon achieved F1 scores of 0.744 for contradiction detection and 0.482 for explanatory-factor identification.
watch_item: Abstract-only analysis may miss important trial details, and explanatory-factor identification remains imperfect; flagged disagreements require expert review.
paper_title: Detecting Contradictory Evidence on Drug-Disease Associations at Scale
